title: Intl minus the clock-reading member: the whole ICU-backed class charges Locale, uniformly, and is refused nowhere
notes: specification/compatibility.mdx, 'Host Globals': the rule is per-operation, not per-object. This is to `Intl` what 20-host-globals/universal-globals-stay-available is to `Math`. ROW FIVE HAS NOW LANDED, and the important thing about this case is that IT DID NOT MOVE. Every member below now publishes `requirements: ["Locale"]` and the stdout is byte-identical to what it was when they published `[]`, because a CHARGE emits no diagnostic and a requirement row is not part of a conformance observation — the harness compares stdout, diagnostics and exit code, and the Go fork's CompileResult protocol carries no rows at all. Both the migration plan and this specification predicted this case would be RETIRED or MOVED by row five landing; measured, it is unchanged, and the reason is worth stating rather than leaving as a silent non-event: the corpus cannot observe rows three or five, so the enforcement of both is pinned by poc/src/language/host-global-allowlist.test.ts ('every ICU-backed member of row five answers identically', which now reads the ROW rather than the diagnostic list) and by nothing here. What this case still guards is the direction that IS observable and is the one a wrong implementation breaks: OVER-REFUSAL. The cheapest wrong implementation of row four or five charges the `Intl` ROOT, which passes 20-host-globals/intl-datetimeformat-construction-needs-a-clock perfectly and silently takes the entire ICU surface of the standard library with it — measured: mutating `root == "Intl" && member == "DateTimeFormat"` to `root == "Intl"` turns ten of these members into SMITHERS1602 and this case red. WHY ROW FIVE CHARGES AND DOES NOT REFUSE: the paragraph under the specification's table supplies the criterion — the ambient spelling is additionally refused only 'where the capability has a source-language surface the author can write instead'. `Locale` is a capability class that exists nowhere in the tree, so a refusal here would name `Locale.context()`, which cannot be written. That is the same criterion that makes `Clock` and `Random` refusals and `Scheduler` a charge. WIDENED 2026-08-28 and the expectation was re-derived by running both backends rather than edited by hand. It used to name two members; §Determinism-Sensitive Members row five used to name four, and the ICU hazard it describes covers THIRTY. This case carries a representative of each shape in it: the nine other `Intl` value members, the four locale-sensitive `String` members, `toLocaleString` on `Number`, `BigInt`, `Array` and a typed array. Both backends produce BYTE-IDENTICAL stdout for all seventeen values, which is the cross-backend half of the claim. ONE THING THE BACKENDS NOW DISAGREE ABOUT, recorded rather than hidden: the reference charges `Locale` here and the Go fork does not. The fork's `rowSet` is keyed by a resolved `*ast.Symbol` and its `addRow` silently drops a symbol-less row, so it cannot represent a requirement for a capability no declaration in the program produces — see the note on `rowSet` in compiler/forkbridge/lowering.go.txt. The disagreement is invisible to this case for exactly the reason stated above, which is why it is written down here. Values whose result IS host ICU data (`RelativeTimeFormat.format`, `DisplayNames.of`, and the two default-locale `toLocaleString`s) are printed as `typeof`, because pinning their text would make this case itself vary with the host's ICU version — which is the hazard row five names. The full thirty-member enumeration lives in poc/src/language/host-global-allowlist.test.ts, which checks rather than runs and so can name the twelve typed arrays and `Float16Array` without depending on the host having them.
